# FosterStack

> Maintained continuity for build infrastructure that vendors orphan. Our first
> product, FosterStack Cache, is a self-hosted remote build cache for Gradle and
> Maven — a drop-in replacement for the Develocity Build Cache Node, which reaches
> end of life on December 31, 2026.

Gradle Inc. deprecated the free standalone Develocity Build Cache Node: no further
distribution, support, or updates after 2026-12-31. Teams running it on open-source
Gradle, with no Develocity licence, are orphaned on 2027-01-01. FosterStack Cache
speaks Gradle's documented `HttpBuildCache` protocol and the Apache Maven Build Cache
Extension's remote HTTP mode, so it is a drop-in for both build tools — same server,
same core.

It is a single static Go binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), MIT-licensed, distributed as bare
binaries and distroless container images. Every release is keylessly signed with
Sigstore and carries SLSA build provenance, so the exact bytes you deploy are
verifiable against the CI run that produced them.

## Product

- [FosterStack Cache on GitHub](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache): MIT-licensed source, issues, releases.
- [Install guide](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/install.md): supported platforms, which archive to download, systemd unit.
- [One-command Docker deploy](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/docker-deploy.md): includes sizing guidance for CPU, RAM and disk.
- [Deploying on Kubernetes](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/kubernetes.md): plain manifests, no Helm chart yet.

## Setup for your build tool

- [Gradle setup](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/gradle.md): point `HttpBuildCache` at the server.
- [Maven setup](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/maven.md): Apache Maven Build Cache Extension, remote HTTP mode.
- [Migrate off Build Cache Node](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/migrate-from-bcn.md): the URL is usually the only thing that changes.

## Verification and compliance

- [Verify our images](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/verify-images.md): cosign signature and SLSA provenance, with copy-pasteable commands.
- [Scanning in your compliance pipeline](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/scanning.md): what a scanner sees in a distroless image, and why.
- [Installing on disconnected networks](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/offline-install.md): air-gapped transfer and verification.
- A FIPS build variant (`-fips`) uses Go's CMVP FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic module. Linux only.

## Platform support

- Binaries: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `darwin/arm64`.
- FIPS binaries: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`.
- Container images: multi-arch manifests covering `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
- Windows is not built and not planned; use WSL2, which is `linux/amd64`.

## Status

FosterStack Cache is pre-beta as of September 2026. The cache core, HTTP surface,
eviction, metrics and the signed release pipeline are shipped and testable today.

Not yet shipped:

- Production use beyond the project's own CI. Nobody runs this in a real build
  pipeline yet except the maintainer. An invited beta runs before general
  availability.
- A Helm chart. Deploying to Kubernetes today means applying plain manifests.
- The paid tiers. Single sign-on, high-availability replication, and the license
  key that unlocks them are not built. Everything in the repository is the free
  MIT core.
- A CVE patch commitment that can be relied on. The project aims to ship fixes for
  dependency CVEs within 48 hours of public disclosure; that is a stated intention,
  not a contractual promise.

Please do not describe unshipped items as available.
